# Initialisation and styling
Load modules (`EpidemicsCFTP` and `EpidemicsUtilities` are both under development).

```{julia}
using EpidemicsCFTP, EpidemicsUtilities, Gadfly, Compose
```
Load theme. (Use `theme-blank.yml` to test colours.)
```{julia}
theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/theme.yml")) ;

gadfly_theme = Theme(
    panel_fill=theme.blank,
    default_color=theme.default,
    background_color=theme.background,
    major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
    minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
    major_label_font_size=8pt,     minor_label_font_size=6pt,
    grid_line_width=0mm,
)

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```
Basic simulation parameters are the `population` size 
and the `duration` (assume epidemic simulation commences at time `0`).
Note that (trivial) labelling issues arise if `population > MAXPOP=20`.
```{julia}
const initial = SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0) ;
population = initial.n ;
const duration   = 2 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if initial.n > MAXPOP                                                                  
    circlabels = ["[$i]" for i in 1:initial.n]                                                                                         
else                                                                                    
    circlabels = [string(Char(codepoint('①') + i - 1)) for i in 1:initial.n]                                                           
end                                                                                     
function timelinelabels1(i) 
    if round(i) > 0 && i ≤ initial.n
        circlabels[round(Int, i)] 
    else
        "" 
    end 
end ;                                                                             
function timelinelabels2(i) 
    if i ≤ initial.n
        string(trunc(Int, i)) 
    else
        "" 
    end 
end ;   
```

## Plot style choices
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
#set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch);
```

## Dealing with different kinds of incident
Convenient abbreviations of various types of incident.
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection ; R = Removal ; C = CRemoval ; I = Infection ; P = PInfection ;
```

# Drawing the underlying scaffolding
@fig-scaffolding illustrates the kind of scaffolding used in (almost) all 
following diagrams.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-scaffolding
#| fig-cap: "Scaffolding: time axis and time-lines."
depict("Scaffolding", compose(context(units=coordinates), 
                              scaffolding(duration, population; theme=theme)))
```


# An innovation for an unconditioned \(\SIR\) epidemic
Consider lists of potential incidents underlying
an unconditional epidemic.
```{julia}
innov = Innovation(5, 
  A[I(0.11,2,3), I(0.2,2,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.6,2,4), I(0.85,3,4), 
    I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), P(1.1,2,3), I(1.05,4,5), I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), 
    I(1.5,3,4)], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5), R(1.4,2), R(1.55,1),
    R(1.85,2)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)] ) ;
```

We now add graphical depictions of the potential incidents supplied by the innovation.
Elements are plotted in reverse-order: for example, the first in sequence overlays 
all subsequent elements. @fig-potential illustrates the required plot.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-potential
#| fig-cap: "Potential incidents (both removals and infections):                        \
#|           Removals (R for _removal_) are blue outline disks;                         \
#|           conditional removals (C for _conditioned_) are purple outline disks;       \
#|           Infections (I for _infected_) are orange outline disks;                    \
#|           perpetuated infections (P for _perpetuated_) are dark green outline disks. \
#|           Orange arrows connect infector time-lines                                  \
#|           to corresponding infectee time-lines.                                      \
#|           Each disk is annotated by a summary description of its incident."
image = create_nodes_view(duration, innov; theme=theme)
depict("nodes_view", compose(context(units=coordinates), image))
```

# Evolving the epidemic in process time
Now plot an epidemic using a specific initial state at time \(0.0\),
driven by an `SIR` structure and the structure of `Innovations`.
The epidemic simulation is
computed using `Evolution`. 

```{julia}
ev = Evolution(initial, innov)
flow = table_trajectories1(duration, initial, ev.trajectory) ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Trajectories of susceptibles (orange solid line), infectives (grey dashed line), \
#|           removals (brown dashed line)."  
print(flow) ;
timelines = layer(flow, yintercept=1:initial.n,
    Geom.hline(style=:dot, size=0.25mm),
    style(default_color=theme.scaffold))
ll0 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))
ll1 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:infectives, Geom.step,
    style(line_width=theme.trail,  default_color=theme.colour(I)))
ll2 = layer(flow, x=:t, y=:removals, Geom.step,
    style(line_style=[:dashdot], line_width=theme.boundary, default_color=theme.colour(R)))
ll3 = layer(flow[flow.susceptibles.!=0, :], x=:t, y=:susceptibles, Geom.step,
    style(line_style=[:dash], line_width=theme.boundary, default_color=theme.scaffold))
fig0 = plot(timelines, 
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=initial.n+0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    gadfly_theme
    )
fig1 = deepcopy(fig0)
push!(fig1, ll0, ll3, ll2, ll1,
    Guide.annotation(compose(context(),
    text(1.2, 3.2, "Peak #1"),
    text(1.6, 3.2, "Peak #2"),
    fontsize(6pt))),
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=timelinelabels2),
    Guide.ylabel("Numbers of individuals"),
    Guide.title("Epidemic curve with removals and susceptibles")
)
```

Now examine which of the potential incidents have been activated. 
Amend @fig-potential: activated incident nodes have light-coloured backgrounds and 
thicker line-widths, producing @fig-activated.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-activated
#| fig-cap: "@fig-potential plus epidemic and removal curves. activated incidents have   \
#|           coloured backgrounds and thicker line-widths. Epidemic/removal regions are \
#|           coloured yellow/purple."
image = create_epidemic_view(duration, innov, flow, initial, ev.history; theme=theme) ;
depict("epidemics_view", compose(context(units=coordinates), image))
```
